- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer below forecast for 3–7 day horizon.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift direction.
- In low-event periods (e.g., <10 events/30d), model tends to underestimate volatility; increase forecast variance or add 0.5–1.5% mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (e.g., 3+ auctions/30d), model overestimates price stability; reduce forecast slope or add 1–2% downward bias for next 5 days.
